author: Reference cases from the implementation report §12.2 (identity, nonaxis rotation, nonsymmetric shear, reflection, singular collapse, zero matrix, zero vector) and boundary cases added for this catalogue. Values were derived by hand as closed forms and evaluated with plain double arithmetic, except where a case says otherwise; every case is cross-checked against tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts, an exact rational oracle that shares no code with the catalogue kernel.
review: No independent human subject reviewer has approved these cases. Automated agreement is engineering evidence only.
semantics: Column-vector convention: M = [[m11, m12], [m21, m22]] acts by M·v, so M·e₁ = (m11, m21) is the first column and M·e₂ = (m12, m22) the second. Every value concerns the matrix with exactly the stored double entries: det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area scale |det M| ≥ 0, orientation from the exact sign of det M (preserved > 0, reversed < 0, collapsed = 0), rank 0/1/2, Δ = (tr M)² − 4·det M, eigen category from the exact sign of Δ and whether M = λ·I (two-real, repeated-scalar, repeated-defective, complex). Eigenvalues are listed λ₁ ≥ λ₂ with multiplicity; eigen-directions are unit vectors whose first nonzero component is positive. The report case [[1, 2], [2, 4]] lies outside the declared entry domain [−3, 3] (m22 = 4); it is represented by [[0.5, 1], [1, 2]], which has the same rank, image line and eigen-directions.
format: Each quantity is keyed by its manifest ID. A number, numeric array or category string means a valid value without an approximation note; {"undefined": CODE} an undefined status with that code; {"limit": "UNDERFLOW"} a numerical limit (a nonzero exact value that rounds to zero); {"value": …, "approximation": "UNDERFLOW"} a valid subnormal value with that note. unitSquareImage lists the images of (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1) in order and whether the polygon is degenerate (det M = 0). An observed number o matches expected e when |o − e| <= absolute + relative·|e|; tolerance 0 is used only when every expected number is the exact value for the stored entries. Categories, codes and statuses always match exactly.

cases.label: Identity: every vector is unchanged; every direction is an unchanged direction
cases.provenance: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; every value is an exact binary fraction; cross-checked exactly against the rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

cases.label: Nonaxis rotation by 30° counterclockwise (irrational entries): area kept, orientation kept, no real unchanged direction
cases.provenance: hand derivation from the exact rotation matrix [[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]] (columns are the rotated e₁ and e₂): det = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1, tr = 2 cos θ, Δ = tr² − 4 = −4 sin²θ < 0 so no real eigen-direction; irrational values evaluate the closed forms in double arithmetic. The stored entries are the nearest doubles to √3/2, so values agree with the stored-entry model only within the declared tolerance; cross-checked against the exact rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

cases.label: Exact boundary: m22 one unit in the last place above 2 makes det = +2^-52, so the matrix is invertible and orientation is preserved, never collapsed
cases.provenance: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; det = 0.5·m22 − 1 is exactly 2^-52 for the stored m22 = 2 + 2^-51; eigenvalues λ₁ = (tr + √Δ)/2 and λ₂ = det/λ₁; directions perturb (1, 2)/√5 and (2, −1)/√5 by about 1e-16; cross-checked against the rational oracle within the declared tolerance

cases.label: Decimal entries [[0.1, 0.7], [0.3, 2.1]]: singular in decimal arithmetic, invertible as stored doubles (det ≈ 4.16e-17 > 0)
cases.provenance: The decimal matrix is singular by hand (second column = 7 × first column). The determinant of the stored doubles is NOT hand-derived: it is the exact rational value of m11·m22 − m12·m21 for the stored entries computed by the rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts), which also fixes λ₂ = det/λ₁. The remaining values are hand closed forms of the decimal matrix (directions (1, 3)/√10 and (7, −1)/√50), within the declared tolerance of the stored-entry values
